samples.question: The picture shows four horizontal SCALES drawn one above the other. Each scale is a dark grey horizontal line carrying short dark grey TICKS that hang below it; the leftmost tick of a scale sits at the left end of its line and the rightmost tick at the right end. The ticks of a scale are NOT evenly spaced, and every scale has its own tick pattern and its own number of ticks. Above each scale stands one solid triangular POINTER; the four pointers are red, green, blue and orange, one to a scale, and each pointer marks the position directly under the middle of its triangle. On every scale, stepping from one tick to the next tick on its right always adds exactly ONE UNIT of value, however wide or narrow that gap looks, and the leftmost tick of a scale reads zero. The VALUE a pointer reads is therefore the number of ticks strictly to its left, plus the fraction of the way it stands across the gap it is in, that fraction being its distance from the tick on its left divided by the whole width of that same gap. Distance in the picture is not value: a pointer standing further to the right, or further from the tick on its left, need not read more. No pointer ever stands on a tick, and no two pointers read the same value. The number of ticks on a scale, the width of the gap a pointer stands in, the pointer's distance from the left end of its scale, its distance from the tick on its left, and how high up the picture its scale is drawn are each the answer no more often than chance allows. Which pointer reads the largest value? Answer red, green, blue or orange.
